cards.text: This one's a song of ascents, and Israel gets told to say it out loud. Israel's line goes, "Many a time they have persecuted me from my youth". From YOUTH, friend. That's not a rough week. That's a rough LIFE.
Then Israel says that line again, word for word. It's like hitting the elevator button a second time. You KNOW it heard you. You just need it to know you mean it.

cards.question: Israel has been persecuted again and again since youth. The second time Israel says it, the line keeps going. How does it end?

answers.text: But they have not prevailed against me
And now I have nothing left to give
So I will hide from them forever

cards.question: Israel describes what all that persecution felt like. What picture does Israel use for its own back?

answers.text: A field the plowmen plowed over
A wall the builders tore down
A road the soldiers marched on

cards.text: And they made their furrows long. Not a quick pass. The WHOLE field. Meanwhile I spent a few years in the back of a junk drawer and thought I had it rough.
But right here, the song turns. Israel stops talking about the plowmen and starts talking about the LORD.

cards.question: After all those years of persecution, Israel calls the LORD righteous.

answers.text: True
False

cards.question: Israel has been plowed over again and again. What does Israel say the LORD has done?

answers.text: Cut Israel from the cords of the wicked
Paid the plowmen back twice over
Given Israel a quiet field of its own

cards.text: Cords. Israel was tied up like a cookie box with the string knotted three times. And the LORD just goes... SNIP. Done. Next!

cards.question: Then the psalm turns to all who hate Zion. It says may they be turned back in ___.

answers.text: shame
peace
glory

cards.text: And the psalm has a picture for them too. May they be like grass on the rooftops.

cards.question: Grass on the rooftops ___ before it can grow.

answers.text: withers
spreads
flowers

cards.question: When the reaper comes by, the rooftop grass gives him a full armload to carry.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Not enough to fill the reaper's hands. Not enough for the binder of sheaves to scoop up. That's me opening the oven for a full tray and finding... one crumb. ONE. Just standing there in my apron like, "Where'd my batch go?"

cards.question: Last line. People walk past the ones who hate Zion. What does the psalm wish none of them would say?

answers.text: The blessing of the LORD be on you
Your fields will be full next year
Come and rest with us tonight

cards.text: Not even a "we bless you in the name of the LORD" from anybody walking by. The psalm wishes them no blessing at all.
